title: Chicken Alfredo
subtitle: garlic butter fettuccine in a big, cheesy Parmesan cream
imageAlt: Fettuccine Alfredo topped with sliced golden chicken and Parmesan
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen chicken breasts? Thaw in the fridge overnight (about 24 h).
Put a big pot of well-salted water on to boil first — it takes the longest.
Measure the Parmesan before you start; the sauce moves fast at the end.
Save 1 cup of pasta water before you drain.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Bring a big pot of water to a boil and salt it well. Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with salt, pepper, garlic powder and Italian seasoning.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the cutlets 5–6 minutes per side until golden and 74°C (165°F) inside. Rest on a board 5 minutes, then slice.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Cook the fettuccine 1 minute less than the box says. Scoop out 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.

steps.title: Make the garlic butter
steps.text: In the same skillet (don't wash it — that's flavour), melt the butter over medium-low. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant, without browning.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Pour in the cream, scrape up the brown bits and simmer gently 3–4 minutes until slightly thickened. Turn the heat to low and whisk in the Parmesan a handful at a time, then garlic powder and pepper. Add mozzarella now if using.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Add the pasta and toss for a minute, loosening with splashes of pasta water until silky. Taste for salt. Top with the sliced chicken and extra Parmesan.

fixIt.fix: The heat was too high when the cheese went in. Take it off the heat, add a splash of pasta water and whisk hard. Next time add cheese on low, a handful at a time.
Loosen with pasta water or a splash of milk, 2 tbsp at a time.
Simmer 1–2 minutes more, or add another ¼ cup Parmesan.
Thinner cutlets cook faster and stay juicy; pull them at 74°C (165°F) and always rest before slicing.

saleTip: Chicken breast club packs are about $13/kg at No Frills; watch for $9–10/kg flyer weeks. Pasta is often 2 for $3–4 — grab extra.
swap: Use shrimp instead of chicken (2 min per side, until pink and opaque), or add roasted broccoli for a veggie.
leftovers: Fridge 3 days. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of milk so the sauce comes back creamy (the microwave can make it oily).
source: Classic Alfredo method (butter, garlic, cream, Parmesan) with pan-seared cutlets; safe temp per Health Canada.
prepAhead: Slice the chicken into cutlets and season up to a day ahead.
Grate/measure the Parmesan and mince the garlic ahead.
reheat: In a pan over low heat with a splash of milk or cream, tossing until hot (74°C / 165°F). The microwave can make Alfredo oily — if you use it, go 50% power and stir often.

basic.note: Butter, garlic, cream and Parmesan — Alfredo at its simplest.

stepNotes.0: Basic: salt, pepper and garlic powder on the chicken.

fancy.note: Silky Alfredo finished with lemon zest and extra Parmesan, crisp-edged chicken and garlic toast.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: finish the sauce with the lemon zest.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Brush baguette slices with butter and garlic powder and toast until golden. Twirl the pasta into nests, fan the sliced chicken on top and shower with Parmesan and black pepper.

plating: Twirl each portion into a nest with tongs and a ladle.
Slice the chicken on the bias and fan it over the top.
Parmesan and pepper from up high.

why.2-2: Cream is the sauce. Milk won't thicken the same way.
why.2-3: Parmesan thickens and seasons — add it off the boil so it melts smoothly.
why.1-0: Cooking the pasta a minute short lets it finish in the sauce without going soft.
